question: Logic says a white shoe supports 'all ravens are black'. How much, on the standard probabilistic answer?
options: Not at all, it is irrelevant
As much as a black raven does
answer: A real but minute amount. 'All ravens are black' is logically equivalent to 'all non-black things are non-ravens', which a white shoe fits, as Hempel noted in 1945. But non-black things vastly outnumber ravens, so checking one of them risks almost nothing. A black raven could have come out white; the shoe never could.
move: Evidence counts for as much as the chance it had of going the other way.
ask: Which of my pieces of evidence would look the same whether I am right or wrong?
trap: Weighing a shoe like a raven, forgetting how many non-black things exist.
reference: Hempel, Studies in the Logic of Confirmation, Mind 54 (213), 1945, pp. 1-26; Hosiasson-Lindenbaum, On Confirmation, Journal of Symbolic Logic 5 (4), 1940
